transcript:
[Doctor]: Hi there, I see you're back for a follow-up visit. What brings you in today?

[Patient]: Hi, Doctor. I've been having this really sharp, shooting pain down my left leg for the past six weeks. It's been getting worse.

[Doctor]: I see, and is there anything else bothering you besides the pain?

[Patient]: Yes, I've also been feeling muscle weakness in my left leg, and it's really affecting my daily activities. Walking, climbing stairs, and even my job as a receptionist have become difficult.

[Doctor]: I'm sorry to hear that. How has this been affecting your sleep?

[Patient]: It's been terrible. I can hardly sleep because of the pain.

[Doctor]: Hmm, that sounds tough. Any recent trauma or accidents that you can recall?

[Patient]: No, nothing like that.

[Doctor]: Alright, let's go over some details. You mentioned the pain has been ongoing for six weeks. Is that correct?

[Patient]: Yes, that's right.

[Doctor]: And you said the pain worsens with prolonged sitting?

[Patient]: Yes, sitting for too long makes it really bad.

[Doctor]: How would you describe the pain? Is it dull, sharp, throbbing?

[Patient]: It's a sharp, shooting pain.

[Doctor]: Got it. And how about the muscle weakness? When did you first notice that?

[Patient]: It started around the same time as the pain, maybe a little bit later.

[Doctor]: Alright. Any other symptoms like fever or chills?

[Patient]: No, just poor sleep because of the pain.

[Doctor]: Let's go through a quick review of systems. For your musculoskeletal system, you mentioned severe sharp pain radiating down the left leg and muscle weakness?

[Patient]: Yes, that's correct.

[Doctor]: For your neurological system, do you have any tingling or numbness?

[Patient]: No tingling or numbness, just the pain and weakness.

[Doctor]: Have you noticed any changes in your strength? Like, is it harder to lift things or walk?

[Patient]: Definitely, my left leg feels weaker.

[Doctor]: Okay. Any issues with your general health, like fever or unexpected weight loss?

[Patient]: No, just poor sleep.

[Doctor]: Alright, let’s move on to the physical exam. Does it hurt when I touch your left leg?

[Patient]: Yes, it’s uncomfortable.

[Doctor]: I see. I'm going to check your range of motion now. Could you try to bend forward for me?

[Patient]: (Attempts to bend) It's very limited and painful.

[Doctor]: Okay, how about leaning backward?

[Patient]: Same thing, it’s quite limited and hurts.

[Doctor]: Alright. I'm going to perform a Straight Leg Raise test. Please let me know if and when you feel pain.

[Patient]: (During the test) Yes, I feel the pain now.

[Doctor]: Okay, that's positive on the left side. Let me check your strength now. Can you push against my hand with your left leg?

[Patient]: (Struggles) It's difficult.

[Doctor]: Alright. Now, I’ll just take your vital signs. Blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, heart rate is 76 bpm, respiratory rate is 16 breaths/min, and temperature is 98.6°F. Everything looks normal there.

[Doctor]: I see we have some pending results. We’re waiting on an X-ray of your lumbosacral spine and a Complete Blood Count. These will help us evaluate the bone structure and rule out any underlying infections.

[Patient]: Okay, sounds good.

[Doctor]: Based on your symptoms and the physical exam, it looks like you have sciatica. This is when the sciatic nerve gets irritated or compressed, causing pain and weakness down your leg.

[Patient]: Oh, I see. That's what I was worried about.

[Doctor]: For treatment, I’m going to prescribe Gabapentin 300 mg, one capsule three times a day for 14 days. That should help with the nerve pain.

[Patient]: Okay, I’ll try that.

[Doctor]: I’m also going to refer you to physical therapy. They can show you some exercises and stretches that will help alleviate your symptoms.

[Patient]: That sounds good. I really need some relief.

[Doctor]: Great. I also recommend some lifestyle modifications. Try to stay active with light walking and gradually increase as you feel better. Make ergonomic adjustments at work to minimize prolonged sitting. And try to reduce your intake of carbohydrates and processed foods.

[Patient]: I can do that. Anything to help.

[Doctor]: Excellent. Let's schedule a follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess your progress and see how effective the treatment plan is. We’ll also review your blood work and X-ray results once they’re available.

[Patient]: Sounds good. I'll be here.

[Doctor]: It's important to manage your pain and adhere to the prescribed medications and physical therapy. If your symptoms don’t improve, we may need to consider further imaging or a specialist referral.

[Patient]: Okay, I understand.

[Doctor]: I’m also providing you with some information on sciatica, its typical course, and management strategies. Remember, follow-up visits and sticking to the treatment plan are crucial for your recovery.

[Patient]: Thanks, Doctor. I’ll make sure to follow everything you’ve recommended.

[Doctor]: Great. Do you have any questions or concerns?

[Patient]: No, I think you’ve covered everything.

[Doctor]: Alright, take care, and we’ll see you in two weeks.

[Patient]: Thank you, Doctor. See you then.
